title: Primitive Distinction Projection Algebra
purpose: Establish the first formal algebraic bridge from the primitive affect/effect distinction condition A|E to its representational distinction projection D(*|*), without introducing D(*|*) as a primitive.

canonical_claims.statement: A|E is the primitive affect/effect distinction condition.
D(*|*) is the formal distinction projection of A|E.
Π_D is a projection operator, not a generative primitive.
Projection preserves representable distinction while not exhausting the full affect/effect condition.

objects.name: Primitive Affect/Effect Distinction Condition
objects.notes: Not interchangeable with A_meta or B_meta.

objects.name: Distinction Projection Operator
objects.definition: Projection from primitive affect/effect distinction condition into formal distinction representation.

laws.name: Distinction Projection Law
laws.meaning: Formal distinction notation arises by projecting the primitive affect/effect distinction condition.

laws.name: Non-Primitivity of Distinction Notation
laws.meaning: The distinction notation is representational and must not be treated as foundational.

laws.name: Projection Non-Exhaustion
laws.meaning: The projection captures representable distinction but not the full primitive condition.

domain_separation.rule: A|E must never be interpreted as A_meta|B_meta or substituted into RT_core bindings.

validation_requirements: No occurrence treats D(*|*) as primitive.

notes: A|E remains governed inside the affect/effect domain and is not a meta-domain binding.
D(*|*) remains a projected whole-expression schema and is not a detached primitive object.
This patch is governance and architecture only.
The projection law is domain-local and does not alter the canonical RT core or the Memory Tensor meta-domain bindings.
σRT remains deferred and is not formalized here.
